item.title: Lion's Head to Platteklip: Weekend heat triggers multiple mountain rescues
item.description: While many Capetonians and visitors spent the weekend soaking up summer sunshine with family and friends, Wilderness Search And Rescue (WSAR) teams were once again stretched across the mountains, responding to multiple incidents in exceptionally hot and demanding conditions, reports Cape {town} Etc.

item.title: Over 2,000 dead in Iran protests as Trump promises help
item.description: Iran's protests lead to a devastating death toll of over 2,000, as US President Donald Trump promises impending support for irate citizens:

item.title: Oh, what a place!
item.description: Welcome back to it. The return to rising and grinding, nine to fiving, crossing T's, dotting I's and chasing down KPIs and ROIs. The inbox is full, the calendar is packed, and the to-do list is already giving side-eye.

item.title: Missing Rikus Kylander achieves five distinctions in matric exams
item.description: 18-year-old Rikus Kylander, who went missing while snorkelling off the coast of Mozambique, has been celebrated by Noordheuwel High School for his remarkable academic achievements:

item.title: South Africa cleared from EU financial watchlist
item.description: South Africa’s standing in the global financial system received a notable boost this week after the European Union confirmed that the country has been removed from its list of high-risk third-country jurisdictions, a move that follows South Africa’s exit from the Financial Action Task Force’s (FATF’s) grey list.

item.title: Cape Town airport breaks passenger record
item.description: Cape Town’s status as one of the world’s most sought-after travel destinations has been underlined by a historic performance at its international airport, which handled a record-breaking 11.1 million two-way passengers in 2025.

item.title: Airlink pauses Hoedspruit flights after flooding
item.description: Airlink has temporarily suspended all flights to and from Hoedspruit in Limpopo after severe flooding left key access roads impassable and restricted operations at the airport, which serves surrounding communities, lodges and the nearby Kruger National Park.

item.title: Western Cape urges disaster declaration
item.description: The Western Cape is facing an unprecedented environmental crisis, with authorities urging the National Disaster Management Centre to declare the province a disaster zone following a severe drought compounded by widespread wildfires.

item.title: Cops who tortured man are still on duty
item.description: Three police officers accused of torturing a barber remain on active duty after SAPS disciplinary action resulted in written warnings. Parliament questions accountability.

item.title: City flags food safety as temperatures rise
item.description: As summer temperatures climb and schools return to full swing, food safety has moved firmly into focus, with the City of Cape Town urging parents and caregivers to take extra care when preparing school lunches and snacks.
